title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'équation des lacets' notes, Grothendieck studies pairs of 2x2 matrices (rho, sigma) over a base ring, up to a common scalar, with fibrewise invertibility. He sets eps0 = -sigma^{-1} rho and eps1 = -rho sigma^{-1}. These are unipotent and generate two unipotent subgroups L0 and L1. They feed the loop formula [alpha,rho] = [beta,sigma] eps1(nu) of §45. The normalisation u1 = Tr(rho+sigma) = 1, i.e. rho+sigma an elementary (rank-1) projector, fixes the scalar ambiguity. The previous page treated the symmetry rho<->sigma, which inverts both eps's.

This page treats the second symmetry, (60): rho'' = rho^{-1}, sigma'' = sigma^{-1}. Then eps0'' = -sigma rho^{-1} = eps1^{-1} and eps1'' = -rho^{-1} sigma = eps0^{-1} (61). So inversion swaps the roles of L0 and L1 up to inversion. This transformation does not preserve the normalisation. Since det eps0 = 1 forces det rho = det sigma = v, and Tr(A^{-1}) = Tr(A)/det A for 2x2 matrices, one gets (62): Tr(rho^{-1}+sigma^{-1}) = u1/v = 1/v. So the normalisation is stable under inversion iff det rho = det sigma = 1 (63). He identifies this as the condition of section 3° of an earlier part (AI, p. 463').

He then discusses the choice of pinning (épinglage) attached to (rho, sigma):
- eps1 is put in the normal form [[1,0],[1,1]].
- eps0 then becomes [[1,u1/v],[0,1]], which is [[1,-1],[0,1]] in the 'modular case', i.e. the standard unipotent generators of SL2(Z) / the congruence-subgroup picture.
- This pinning depends on the order of (rho, sigma): swapping them replaces eps1 by eps1^{-1}.
- There are four 'natural' pinnings, attached to the sections eps0^{±1}, eps1^{±1} of the pair of unipotent group schemes.

On the next page he justifies preferring eps1 (and L1) by the form of the loop equation. Overall the page is bookkeeping of the S3 × Z/2-type symmetry group of the triple (rho^{-1}, sigma, eps0) with product 1, i.e. the monodromy triple at infinity, 1, 0 of P^1 minus 3 points. He checks how normalisations and pinnings transform under it.
errors: No mathematical errors found. Formulas (61) and (62) check out, given that det rho = det sigma follows from eps0 being unipotent.

Minor observation: in the modular case u1/v = -1 with u1 = 1 gives v = det rho = -1. So condition (63) fails there, and the normalisation is not inversion-stable in the modular case. The page does not comment on this.

ideas.what: Action of inversion (rho, sigma) -> (rho^{-1}, sigma^{-1}) on the unipotent pair (eps0, eps1): it exchanges them up to inversion. The trace normalisation is preserved iff det = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Symmetries of monodromy triples / rank-2 local systems on P^1 minus {0,1,inf} (S3 and dual action); normalisation of rigid hypergeometric-type triples
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann, Klein, Fricke); modern rigid local systems: Katz, Levelt

ideas.what: Choice of pinning: put eps1 in the form [[1,0],[1,1]], so eps0 = [[1,u1/v],[0,1]]. Four natural pinnings correspond to eps0^{±1}, eps1^{±1}.
ideas.modern_name: Pinning (épinglage) of a pair of opposite unipotent subgroups; standard generators of SL2(Z)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (notion of épinglage in general; not this specific application)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping of symmetries and normalisations within Grothendieck's unpublished 'équation des lacets' work. The only mild historical interest is the explicit discussion of the four natural pinnings and the choice of L1, continued on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Cross-reference reads more like 'de (AI)fr (p. 463')' rather than 'p. 363''.
First line of the remark: the handwriting has 'Tr(ρ''+σ'')=1' (the second term looks like a malformed sigma'').
'(par un calcul matriciel immédiat)' is correct; 'déjà' is an insertion above 'bien sûr'.
